name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: New D+7 district from redistricting favors McGuire
Polymarket prices McGuire at roughly 96% to win
McGuire leads in fundraising and outside support
No public polling; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The redrawn district leans Democratic by seven points, McGuire has out-raised the incumbent while holding a large outside-spending edge, and prediction markets price him near-certain; nothing in the record points to an upset.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing Gallagher competitive in the inland, more Republican portion of the new district would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's redrawn 1st District combines the Democratic-leaning North Coast with the northern Sacramento Valley, producing a seven-point Democratic partisan lean. State Senator Mike McGuire faces Assemblymember James Gallagher, who advanced to the general election as the nominal incumbent under the state's top-two system. No public general-election polls are available, and national race raters have not listed the contest.

The evidence that exists favors McGuire. He has out-raised Gallagher and holds a wide edge in outside spending, while prediction markets price his win probability near 96%. The 2026 national environment also tilts toward Democrats. The forecast makes McGuire a strong favorite; the chief uncertainty is the lack of polling in a district where Gallagher's name recognition inland could keep the result closer than fundamentals imply.
